newsitem.title: USA: Compaq comfortable with Q4 estimates - CFO.
newsitem.headline: Compaq comfortable with Q4 estimates - CFO.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp is "comfortable" with analysts' estimates that it will earn $1.54 per share in the fourth quarter of 1996, Chief Financial Officer Earl Mason said on Tuesday.
"Total average estimates for the street average out to $1.54 (a share) and we're comfortable with all that," Mason told Reuters in an interview.
Mason would not comment on the company's sales during the Christmas season, but he did say that sales of the firm's new handheld computers were "very good."

In November, Compaq president Eckhard Pfeiffer told Reuters that sales of the small computer, the PC Companion, had exceeded expectations and that the company was "scrambling" to increase production for the holiday shopping season.

Compaq said on Tuesday it had formed a finance unit, Compaq Capital Corp, to offer customer leasing and financing options. Mason said the new unit, to be operating by the end of the second quarter of this year, had been created in part because Compaq customers "want to find ways to lower their total cost of ownership."
He would not disclose the company's projections for how much it might add to sales. Mason said the unit would be capitalized "properly" but that the amount of funding was still under study.

Irving Rothman, who was named president of Compaq Capital, said the unit would initially focus on commercial customers in the North American market, but eventually would "offer financial products and services across a broad spectrum of Compaq customers, and worldwide.
"We hope to drive customer behavior by providing an incentive on the financial side for them to buy and use Compaq products and services," he said.
Rothman formerly was with AT&T, where he was group president of AT&T Capital Corp.
Mason would not comment on how sales of computers equipped with Intel Corp's new MMX multimedia chips were going. Systems based on the chip went on sale last week.
